title: Higher-order functions
hints: A value of type `IntFunc` is called like any function: `f(x)`. To *return* a function, return a function literal: `return func(x int) int { ... }`.

`ApplyN`: loop `n` times (`for range n`) and reassign `x = f(x)` each time; ranging over `n <= 0` does nothing. `Compose`: the literal's body computes `f(g(x))`, and it can use `f` and `g` because closures capture them.
`Compose` is `return func(x int) int { return f(g(x)) }`. `Twice(f)` is just `Compose(f, f)`.
